# windows_eventlog (Resource)

Manages the size and retention policy of an existing Windows event log on a remote Windows host via SSH and PowerShell (the .NET `EventLogConfiguration` API: `Get-WinEvent -ListLog` plus `SaveChanges()`). A log always exists — Windows or the owning feature creates it — so creating this resource never provisions anything new: it only tunes the log's settings in place, and deleting it makes no remote change unless `restore_on_destroy` is set.

Both classic logs (`Application`, `System`, `Security`) and modern channels (`Microsoft-Windows-PowerShell/Operational`, matched literally — the `/` is part of the name, never a path) are supported. Only the attributes configured in Terraform are written; every other setting on the host is left untouched and undiffed. `record_count` and `file_size_bytes` are observed informational values and never produce drift.

Group Policy owns the `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\EventLog` view: when a GPO manages a log, the observed values can diverge from what Terraform writes at the next policy refresh, which is reported through `policy_override` with a warning on every apply.

Shrinking `maximum_size_bytes` below the current file size is accepted by Windows (it applies after the next clear or archive): the apply warns instead of failing.

Import format: `<log name>` (exact, e.g. `Application` or `Microsoft-Windows-PowerShell/Operational`).

## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    windows = {
      source  = "kfrlabs/windows"
      version = "~> 0.1"
    }
  }
}

provider "windows" {
  host     = var.windows_host
  username = var.windows_username
  password = var.windows_password
}

# Tune the Application log in place: grow the maximum size and archive the
# log instead of overwriting when it fills. Only the configured attributes
# are assigned before SaveChanges(); everything else on the host is left
# untouched. The log always exists, so this resource never provisions
# anything new — and destroy makes no remote change unless
# restore_on_destroy re-applies the pre-existing values captured at
# creation time.
resource "windows_eventlog" "application" {
  name               = "Application"
  maximum_size_bytes = 1073741824 # 1 GiB (multiple of 64 KiB, at least 1 MiB)
  retention          = "archive"  # overwrite | archive | retain

  restore_on_destroy = true

  # Bound every remote operation explicitly: without this block each
  # operation defaults to 5 minutes, and a stalled PowerShell/SSH session
  # then surfaces a timeout diagnostic instead of blocking Terraform
  # indefinitely.
  timeouts = {
    create = "5m"
    read   = "5m"
    update = "5m"
    delete = "5m"
  }
}

# A modern channel name contains "/": it is matched literally, never as a
# path. Enabling a disabled Analytic or Debug channel clears it.
resource "windows_eventlog" "powershell" {
  name               = "Microsoft-Windows-PowerShell/Operational"
  enabled            = true
  maximum_size_bytes = 268435456 # 256 MiB
}

output "application_size_bytes" {
  value       = windows_eventlog.application.maximum_size_bytes
  description = "Maximum size of the Application log file, in bytes."
}

output "powershell_enabled" {
  value       = windows_eventlog.powershell.enabled
  description = "Whether the PowerShell Operational channel is enabled."
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Exact event log name (`LogName`), matched literally (never as a wildcard). Classic logs (`Application`, `System`, `Security`) and modern channels (`Microsoft-Windows-PowerShell/Operational`, where `/` is part of the name) are both valid. Immutable after creation (ForceNew); the log always exists on the host.

### Optional

- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the log is enabled (`IsEnabled`). Classic logs cannot be disabled: setting `false` on one fails with an `unsupported` error. Disabling an Analytic or Debug channel clears it.
- `log_file_path` (String) Path of the event log file (`LogFilePath`). Absolute or `%SystemRoot%`-based; the directory must exist on the host (validated host-side).
- `maximum_size_bytes` (Number) Maximum size of the event log file, in bytes. Must be a multiple of 64 KiB and at least 1 MiB. Sizes above 4 GiB warn on classic logs.
- `restore_on_destroy` (Boolean) When `true`, destroy re-applies the pre-existing log values captured at creation (or import) time. Defaults to `false`: destroy makes no remote change.
- `retention` (String) What happens when the log reaches its maximum size. One of `overwrite` (oldest events are overwritten, `Circular`), `archive` (the full log is archived and a new one started, `AutoBackup`), `retain` (stop logging when full, `Retain`; plan warns on the `Security` log because the host can halt when `CrashOnAuditFail` is set).
- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `file_size_bytes` (Number) Current size of the log file on disk, in bytes. Informational only: never produces drift.
- `id` (String) Resource identifier. Set to the exact event log name.
- `is_classic_log` (Boolean) Whether the log is a classic log (`Application`, `System`, `Security`, ...). Classic logs cannot be disabled.
- `log_type` (String) Log type as reported by the host (`Administrative`, `Operational`, `Analytic` or `Debug`).
- `policy_override` (Boolean) Whether Group Policy carries `MaxSize`, `Retention` or `AutoBackupLogFiles` for this log (`HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\EventLog\<log>`). When `true`, the GPO value wins at the next policy refresh and Terraform-managed values may diverge.
- `record_count` (Number) Number of records currently in the log. Informational only: never produces drift.

<a id="nestedatt--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
- `delete` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Setting a timeout for a Delete operation is only applicable if changes are saved into state before the destroy operation occurs.
- `read` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Read operations occur during any refresh or planning operation when refresh is enabled.
- `update` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import an event log by exact name (classic or modern channel — the "/"
# in a channel name is part of the name). Logs always exist, so import only
# adopts the live settings into state; nothing is created. The observed
# values become the snapshot for a later restore_on_destroy.
terraform import windows_eventlog.application 'Application'
terraform import windows_eventlog.powershell 'Microsoft-Windows-PowerShell/Operational'
```
